text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- About 1,000 people, most of them pensioners, gathered near the government building to show their scorn for a one lat rise in pensions to an average 40.50 lats.

- The U.N. General Assembly is to discuss a draft resolution on the observation of human rights in Latvia and Estonia which was submitted by Russia. The alternative drafts prepared by Latvia and Estonia had been submitted a few hours earlier.

- The government parties recommended that Minister of Environment Protection and Regional Development and Deputy Prime Minister Anatoli Gorbunovs head the Latvian side in a commission with Russia that deals with relations between the two countries.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele proposed postponing the cabinet's plans to make government more efficient until after next year's budget has been adopted.
- The parliament's foreign affairs committee has prepared a draft resolution criticising Belarus's President Lukashenko and voicing support to the Belarus parliament.
- According to Janis Karpovichs, a member of the Riga City Council, 50,000 people in Riga are freezing in their flats.
- India has responded to Latvia's note to show leniency when dealing with the case of five Latvian pilots arrested on charges of supplying weapons to guerrillas in the region of Bengal.
- The parliament faction of the right-wing Fatherland & Freedom party sent their greetings to the Chechen people on the occassion of their victory over "Russian colonisers".
- The Latvian Privatization Agency has been commissioned with buying the Swedish stake in the Latvian-Swedish joint venture Baltic Terminal.
- The Latvian Ports Council approved next year's development budget of one million lats.
- Unibanka announced a two percent reduction in credit interest rates from December 1.
